title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Eighth edition, Volume 6, Burning glasses-Climate - EB.16
text: Arsenic acid,ASO<sub>2</sub> is volatile its vapor has non smell, unless when heated on, charcoal, when it is reduced to the metallic state, and it is the metallic vapour the smell of which is then observed. It is surprisingly soluble in water and its solution gives, with excess of lime-water, a white precipitate of arsenice of lime, with mamoniaco-sulphate or copper, a grass-green precipitate of arsenice of copper. Scheed’s green with ammonico-nitrite of silver, a demonyline precipitate of arsenice of silver and with hydronal- phuric acid, bright blue sulpholment, AAS<sub>2</sub>. By these clar-acterics this substance when pure is easily recognised i; and from its very poisonous nature, and the facility of presence it, poisoning by its means is so frequent, that it has to be sought for different than any other poison.
